summary: The candidate is a verified narrow fix for the reported 3072-versus-6144 mixed-precision shared-expert load mismatch. It is not a full fix for serving GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on SM120 because the separate DSA dependency/backend architecture gap remains.

tests.what_was_measured: On the recorded base, the published shared-expert exclusion matched, routed experts remained included, and the loader gate incorrectly returned no disable reason.
Exact candidate regression and neighboring GLM fusion-gate behavior: 4 passed.
Existing GLM-5 NextN ModelOpt behavior: 3 passed, 2 subtests passed.
Reported wildcard, single sparse layer, dense-layer boundary, both-excluded, uniform-FP4, and forced-fusion cases all produced the required decisions.
Python syntax and patch whitespace integrity.

gpu_execution.evidence: The relevant tests exercise the pre-construction loader decision and require no GPU kernel. The available device was one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950, not the required eight NVIDIA SM120 GPUs.

remaining_counterexamples: After bypassing the loader mismatch, the reported SM120 serving configuration can still fail in released FlashInfer/DeepGEMM DSA paths with an unsupported-architecture error.
TP=8 full-model loading and generation with nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 were not independently exercised because the required SM120 hardware and weights were unavailable.
remaining_limitations: Prepared hardware was a single AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2, not eight RTX PRO 6000 SM120 GPUs with CUDA 13.
No NVIDIA NVFP4, DSA, CUDA graph, full serving, or multi-node path was validated.
No native source changed in the candidate, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
